channel.title: MakeBiz Group News
channel.description: AI agents, CRM, automation and servers: practical notes from MakeBiz Group, Dubai.

item.title: Why AI forgets everything and how memory fixes it
item.description: A regular assistant remembers only the conversation window. If you move memory into a database and return facts to the context, an agreement from a month ago stays with the agent

item.title: What an AI agent is and how it differs from a chatbot
item.description: A chat answers a question and forgets. An agent has a role, memory, and access to systems: it launches the process itself, drives it through to a result, and reports back. We will illustrate this using the example of a sales department, where eight roles hand off work along a chain

item.title: Where the sales team loses a client during a call
item.description: The problem is not the number of calls, but that the business does not hear at which stage the conversation breaks down. What analyzing all calls by script stage gives you

item.title: Meetings happen, but decisions get lost: what to do about it
item.description: Transcription of an hour-long meeting, analysis, conclusions and tasks. How to make sure agreements land in the system automatically, rather than in the memory of one person

item.title: Why AI makes things up, and how to solve it architecturally
item.description: Hallucinations, the main risk of AI in sales and documents. We break down our approach: facts come only from a verified database, documents are assembled by a generator, not the model

item.title: Supplier comparison: how to stop reconciling price lists by hand
item.description: Quotes arrive as PDFs, scans, and emails, while you have to compare them in Excel. What extracting price, lead time, and availability from any document delivers

item.title: Why CRM data drifts apart, and how to fix it
item.description: A classic problem: everyone writes in their own way. The solution is simple but not obvious - a single point of record through which all changes flow

item.title: Services go down at night: how the system fixes itself
item.description: The watchdog checks services every couple of minutes, restarts anything that has gone down, and messages the owner if something did not come back up. Plus rollback to any point

item.title: Company data and AI: what stays with you and what leaves
item.description: The main business question before implementation. We break down what self-hosted means and why it changes the conversation about security

item.title: One entry point, dozens of specialists: how the orchestrator works
item.description: A person writes as usual, and inside the Conductor understands the request and brings up the right roles. Why this is more convenient than ten different bots

item.title: Where to start with AI implementation so you do not waste money
item.description: Not just install AI, but analyze the process and match roles to a specific pain point. Why diagnostics matter more than technology
